method: The closing pass for the .py blind spot described in docs/gaps.md. Three signals: code containing 'exaloop/codon/releases/download' (73 files), 'codon run -release' (62 files), and 'from codon import' in Python (54 files). Deduplicated against all 84 round-1 candidates.
result: 58 repositories that round 1 could not see. Every one of them is new; the overlap with round 1 was zero, which means the extension:codon enumeration and the invocation signals find disjoint populations rather than the same one.
caveat: These are CANDIDATES at confidence low. None has been opened. Classes below are provisional readings of the search hit alone.
signal_note: 'from codon import' in Python is almost useless on its own: 53 of its 54 hits are genetics code importing a local module named codon, and the single real hit (suzukiiichiro/N-Queens) was already known. The two Codon-specific signals -- the release URL and the run invocation -- carry the whole yield.

classes.note: Distribution packaging of Codon itself: package definitions, version trackers and Nix flakes. NOT users. Mostly forks -- roughly twenty are copies of termux-packages carrying the same codon/build.sh, the same shape as the newnem.codon problem in the genetics false positives. Needs a fork-dedup rule before any of it is counted.
Exaloop's own. Should sit with the anchors rather than in a user class.

Four more UVic CSC427 students, taking that course to twelve repos, plus velvetc which carries the same actions.yml harness under a different name. A THIRD course also appears: NYCU object-oriented Python, whose notes carry a Codon chapter, in two copies.

The substantive part of the round. GeneticEngine is a genetic-programming framework whose example runner invokes Codon; word-counter and University compare Codon against other implementations; atcoder-codon packages a competitive-programming environment around it; EPlusPlus ships a Codon installer written in Rust.
Blogs, notebooks, notes and starred-readme collections.
